properties.name: Fort Glenn Army Airfield (Umnak)
properties.operator_1939_1945: USAAF Eleventh Air Force; RCAF 111(F) Sqn; USN detachment
properties.runway_specs: Three Marston-mat & gravel runways (up to 7,000 ft) at Otter Point / Northeast Umnak
properties.notes: Secretly built early 1942 under 'Blair Packing Co.' cover; first wheeled combat airfield in Aleutians; P-40s surprised Japanese raiders attacking Dutch Harbor Jun 3-4, 1942.
properties.modern_equivalent: Abandoned / Fort Glenn National Historic Landmark
properties.proof_summary: USACE Green Book IV, US Army CMH, and Alaska WWII Army Airfields verify May 1942 operational readiness and exact Fort Glenn coordinates (53°22'39"N 167°53'31"W).
properties.title: Fort Glenn Army Airfield (Umnak)

properties.name: Driftwood Bay Auxiliary Strip
properties.operator_1939_1945: USAAF Eleventh Air Force; U.S. Army Coast Artillery outpost
properties.runway_specs: 3,500 ft coastal gravel auxiliary/emergency strip 12 mi NW of Dutch Harbor
properties.notes: Auxiliary emergency & coastal surveillance strip on NW Unalaska Island supporting Dutch Harbor and Umnak air operations 1942-45 (later Cold War White Alice station).
properties.proof_summary: Exact airfield coordinates verified from SkyVector/Wikipedia AK23 (53°58'19"N 166°51'26.6"W) and Alaska DEC FUDS record.
properties.title: Driftwood Bay Auxiliary Strip

properties.name: Atka Auxiliary Airfield
alternate_names: Atka Air Force Auxiliary Field / NAAF Atka
properties.operator_1939_1945: USAAF Eleventh Air Force; U.S. Navy Auxiliary Air Facility
properties.runway_specs: Marston-mat emergency fighter strip & seaplane anchorage on Nazan Bay
properties.notes: USAAF landed Sep 16, 1942 to build fighter/medium bomber support strip against Kiska; Navy NAAF active Feb-Sep 1943 before decommissioning as combat moved past Adak/Amchitka.
properties.modern_equivalent: PAAK / Atka Airport (Modern strip nearby; WWII strip FUDS)
properties.proof_summary: USACE DERP-FUDS Atka report explicitly dates USAAF landing Sep 16, 1942, Navy NAAF Feb 13, 1943, and decommissioning Sep 1, 1943.
primary_sources: USACE Atka Auxiliary Field DERP-FUDS Assessment (2006)
properties.title: Atka Auxiliary Airfield

properties.name: Adak Army Airfield (Davis AAF)
properties.operator_1939_1945: USAAF Eleventh Air Force; U.S. Navy NOB Adak
properties.runway_specs: Initial 10-day Marston-mat strip (Sep 1942) expanded to two paved runways (7,500 ft & 6,000 ft)
properties.notes: Occupied Aug 30, 1942; 807th Engineer Aviation Bn drained Sweeper Cove lagoon and launched first combat raid on Kiska Sep 14, 1942; major Aleutian command & bomber base through 1945.
properties.proof_summary: NHHC Aleutians Campaign, USN BuDocks Ch. 23, and Alaska WWII Army Airfields confirm Aug 30, 1942 landing and Sep 1942 combat launch. Coordinates match PADK.
properties.title: Adak Army Airfield (Davis AAF)
